why_this_exists: The allowance lives in ONE row, ingestion_state.bettor_live_probe_state,
and `obs-arm` replaces it wholesale with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. Replacing
a row is not preserving its history: the moment a replacement probe is
armed, every trace of this one is gone from the database. This file is
the copy, written BEFORE that happens.
This is the SECOND such record. The first is probe-12724d1e.json.
outcome: NEVER RAN. Failed on its own first reservation and spent nothing.

defect.summary: The reservation UPDATE named a column the table does not have.
detail: ctl.reserve() wrote `SET value = jsonb_set(...), updated_at = now()`.
ingestion_state, created by backend/migrations/001_init.sql, has exactly
two columns: key TEXT PRIMARY KEY and value JSONB NOT NULL. There is no
updated_at. Postgres rejected the statement inside the reservation
transaction, so the reservation raised rather than returning a verdict,
and the loop treated an uncertain reservation as a refusal -- correctly.

no_schema_change_is_required: The repair is to stop writing a column that does not exist. Production
schema is correct as it stands; the code was wrong about it.

the_cause_we_need_to_eliminate.statement: Our code and fixtures did not match the production interfaces.
not: This was not 'an environment issue'. Calling it one obscures the cause.
Nothing about the production environment was unusual, misconfigured or
unavailable. Production behaved exactly as its schema and its call
signatures specify. What was wrong was on our side: the code assumed
interfaces production does not have, and the fixtures were built from
the same assumptions, so they could never contradict it.

the_rule_that_follows: A proof is worth nothing if it supplies the seam it is meant to test.
Fixtures must be derived from the production artifact -- the migration,
the real entry point, the real image -- not authored alongside the code
